stem: A client who has been stable on theophylline starts erythromycin. Several days later the client develops persistent nausea, tremor, palpitations, and tachycardia. Which nursing action is most appropriate?

options.A: Continue theophylline at the current dose and treat the nausea symptomatically, because erythromycin generally lowers theophylline exposure and reduces toxicity risk.
options.B: Withhold additional theophylline doses and obtain a serum theophylline concentration promptly because erythromycin can inhibit theophylline metabolism and reduce its clearance.
options.C: Increase the theophylline dose to offset reduced bronchodilator effect, because erythromycin accelerates theophylline metabolism and can lower the serum concentration.
options.D: Continue both medications and recheck the pulse after the antibiotic course, because tremor and tachycardia are expected bronchodilator effects that do not require drug-level evaluation.

rationale: Current DailyMed labeling identifies erythromycin as a drug that inhibits theophylline metabolism and can decrease theophylline clearance. The label instructs that when a patient receiving theophylline develops nausea, vomiting, or other signs or symptoms consistent with theophylline toxicity, additional theophylline doses should be withheld and a serum theophylline concentration measured immediately. The label also reports fine skeletal-muscle tremor, palpitations, sinus tachycardia, and cardiac arrhythmias among theophylline adverse effects. Therefore B is correct. A and C reverse the direction of the erythromycin interaction. D minimizes a cluster of findings that warrants prompt drug-level evaluation.
educational_objective: Recognize erythromycin as an inhibitor of theophylline metabolism and respond to suspected theophylline toxicity by withholding additional doses and obtaining a serum concentration promptly.
source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine
source_locator: Warnings > Drug Interactions: adding a drug that inhibits theophylline metabolism, including erythromycin, can reduce clearance. Warnings > When Signs or Symptoms of Theophylline Toxicity Are Present: when nausea/vomiting or other toxicity symptoms occur, withhold additional theophylline doses and measure a serum concentration immediately. Adverse Reactions: fine skeletal-muscle tremor, palpitations, sinus tachycardia and cardiac arrhythmias are reported.
source_claim_supported: Erythromycin can inhibit theophylline metabolism and reduce clearance; suspected theophylline toxicity requires withholding additional doses and immediate serum-concentration measurement.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed pp. 38–41: identify medication interactions, monitor therapeutic drug levels, evaluate client response to medication, recognize adverse effects, and intervene when toxicity is suspected.
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — erythromycin-theophylline interaction and toxicity response
correction_summary: Rebuilt all four actions so the keyed response is no longer uniquely longest and the distractors test realistic errors in interaction direction, dose escalation, and delayed toxicity evaluation.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Methylxanthine therapy — erythromycin interaction and theophylline toxicity
audit_findings.stem: PASS — provides stable baseline theophylline use, addition of a known interacting drug, and a coherent toxicity symptom cluster.
audit_findings.option_A: PASS as distractor — symptomatic treatment may be appropriate adjunctively, but erythromycin inhibits rather than accelerates theophylline metabolism and toxicity evaluation cannot be deferred.
audit_findings.option_B: PASS — directly matches the current label's interaction and immediate response to suspected toxicity; uniquely best.
audit_findings.option_C: PASS as distractor — it reverses the interaction direction and would increase exposure in a client already showing toxicity symptoms.
audit_findings.option_D: PASS as distractor — tremor, palpitations and tachycardia are recognized adverse effects and, with persistent nausea after an interacting drug is added, warrant prompt level assessment rather than delayed observation.
audit_findings.ambiguity: PASS — B is the only option that both interprets the erythromycin interaction correctly and follows the labeled toxicity response.
audit_findings.second_answer: EXCLUDED — A and C reverse or minimize the interaction; D delays evaluation despite a toxicity-compatible symptom cluster.
audit_findings.cueing: PASS — the keyed option is not the longest and all alternatives are comparable in clinical detail and syntax.
audit_findings.blueprint: PASS — NCSBN Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies directly includes drug interactions, therapeutic drug monitoring, and toxicity response.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — challenged whether symptoms could be nonspecific or merely expected bronchodilator effects; the label explicitly instructs immediate serum measurement and dose withholding whenever toxicity-compatible symptoms occur, even if another cause is suspected, leaving B uniquely correct.
